approaches.name: satellite imagery, CAPI and machine learning for survey sampling and data quality
approaches.description: Uses satellite imagery, IDP registries and tracking data to build sampling frames, CAPI with GPS for fieldwork, and ML to impute missing consumption data. To achieve this objective, the project will concentrate efforts in i) improvements to the M&E toolkit, ii) developing a dashboard for enhanced monitoring capabilities, and ii) providing specialized training to relevant stakeholders.
The NDP9 envisages that the national M&E system will be built around a periodic reporting system based on indicators at the output and outcome levels.
Additionally, a basic dashboard to compare efficacy, efficiency, and quality of public programs and policies by pillars and sectors under the NDP9 will be developed.

To enhance the quality of data collection, a combination of CAPI and Real-time Data Monitoring (RTDM) tools will be used to reduce errors prior to and during data collection and to evaluate performance of enumerators while conducting fieldwork.

The quality of data collected via CAPI will be monitored real time using RTDM where key statistics will be produced and updated every day by enumerators to detect any mistakes or wrong doings by them.
As soon as such mistakes and wrong doings are detected, enumerators will be alerted by supervisors or the headquarters.

In the absence of a recent population census, the sampling frame will be based on a combination of urban primary sampling units demarcated for the purposes of PESS and rural primary sampling units derived from an updated sampling frame based on satellite imagery.
This activity will update the sampling frame, from which a sample will be selected using a standard two stage sampling method.

The sampling frame for IDPs will be created from the satellite images and household registries for IDP camps in Central Regions, Jubaland Administration, South West Administration, Galmudug, Puntland, Somaliland as well as in Banadir.
This project will update the sampling frame for urban areas and rural areas to address the shortcomings of the PESS sampling frame and add the sampling frame for nomads and IDPs.
The tracking data generated from the second wave of the SHFS can be exploited to construct the sampling frame for nomads.
Nomads represent an estimated 25 percent of the Somali population according the PESS and their inclusion in the sampling frame is necessary to ensure representativeness of future surveys.

SHFS covers 236 items (110 food items, 89 non-food items, and 37 durables) and to save time, each household does not have to report around 20 items, expenditures of which will be imputed using a Machine Learning technique.
Data collection will involve face-to-face interviews using CAPI.
For example, CAPI can include built- in validation that prompts alerts to interviewers when they enter potential outliers or commit mistakes.
Furthermore, supervision is facilitated by CAPI since the devices can be integrated with GPS tracking and early data transfer allows supervisors to monitor results and offer faster feedback.

Emerging challenges require a modern and adaptive approach to data collection, but there is currently no data collection system in place to respond quickly to new and more immediate data needs for policy.

Somali policy makers are operating in a volatile context with very limited data, thus a frequent and rapid monitoring system that can provide almost real-time data even in emergency situations is important to support timely policy responses.
Insecurity in part of the country also continue to hinder data collection requiring less conspicuous methods of data collection.
